item.title: Britannia Q2 net profit rises 10.8% to ₹726 crore on volume growth
item.description: Bakery food company Britannia Industries Ltd on Thursday reported an increase of 10.82 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 725.99 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis, led by volume growth. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 655.06 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Britannia Industries. Britannia Industries' revenue from the sale of products was up 16.6 per cent to Rs 5,541.57 crore in the September quarter. The sales growth was "led by volume growth of 13 per cent", said Britannia Industries in its earnings statement. Its revenue from operations was up 15.64 per cent to Rs 5,597.79 crore in the second quarter of FY27. It was at Rs 4,840.63 crore in the corresponding quarter. Britannia's total expenses were at Rs 4,690.47 crore, up 17 per cent in Q2, FY27. Its total income, which includes other income, was up 15.9 per cent to Rs 5,671.30 crore in the September quarter. item.description: Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran has met Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni at Palazzo Chigi in Rome, with the acquisition of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group by Tata Motors featuring prominently in discussions amid growing strategic industrial and economic ties between the two countries. Sources said Chandrasekaran presented the Tata Group's strategy following the Indian conglomerate's acquisition of a controlling stake in Iveco Group, one of Italy's leading commercial vehicle manufacturers, at the meeting held on Wednesday. The meeting came amid the increasing strategic economic and industrial collaboration between Italy and India.
